brief.summary: An in-house forecasting workbook built for the treasury department of a large regional hospital network, where the treasury team jointly maintains the rolling 13-week cash forecast each week.
brief.user: Helen Szabo, a senior treasury analyst who owns the consolidation of the weekly forecast. She has been in treasury for nine years, knows which colleagues own which cash lines, and answers to the Assistant Treasurer, who alone can lock and publish a forecast.
brief.moment: It's Wednesday at 1:15 pm and the forecast locks at 3:00 pm. Two colleagues are working in it right now: Raj is updating payroll for a retro pay adjustment and Tomás is revising vendor disbursements. Since last week's version, someone cut patient-collections receipts for weeks 3–5 by $4.2M, which drops the week-5 ending balance below the $25M minimum-liquidity line. Helen needs to find out who made that change and why, resolve Tomás's open question about the capital equipment payment timing, make sure nobody overwrites Raj's payroll lines while he's in them, and get the forecast to a state Kathleen can sign off.
brief.data: Forecast for weeks of Nov 16, 2026 – Feb 8, 2027 across 4 entities (Mercy Ridge Medical Center, Lakeshore Community Hospital, Physician Group, Shared Services). 22 cash lines, including patient collections, Medicare and Medicaid remittances, payroll (biweekly, about $38M per cycle), vendor AP, debt service, capital expenditures and intercompany sweeps, each with an owner, a weekly amount and a variance from last week's version. Roles: 5 analysts (edit their own lines), 2 revenue-cycle liaisons (edit collections only), Assistant Treasurer Kathleen Moore (lock and publish), CFO office (read only). Current week-5 projected ending balance: $22.7M against a $25M floor.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
